Blade.Description: A sharp object that can pierce through objects if the material is durable and strong.

KeyButton.Description:
Sends trigger signals when activated by a player.
When connected to a seat and the input key is configured/configureed, the player sitting in the seat can activate the button by pressing the corresponding key.

1.Description: The name of the key that will trigger this button when the key is pressed by players in connected seats.
1.Name: Key

3.Description: Determines how trigger signals will be emitted. Emit mode sends trigger signals to attached parts. Self mode only triggers the part internally.
3.Name: SignalMode

2.Description: Determines the type of key event to trigger this button on.
2.Name: PressMode

ClickButton.Description: Sends trigger signals when activated by a player.

1.Description: Determines how trigger signals will be emitted. Emit mode sends trigger signals to attached parts. Self mode only triggers the part internally.
1.Name: SignalMode

Hull.Description: Is able to float in the water, as well as carry objects attached to it. Primarily used for creating boats and other water craft.

Door.Description: When triggered, it will open, and if triggered again will close.

1.Description: Determines if the door is open.
1.Name: Switch

Wood.Description: **A natural resource found in trees and flora.** It is a simple and yet effective material that is used for simple objects and structures. These can be mainly found in terra and forest planets, but can occasionally be found in temperate tundra and desert planets.

DelayWire.Description: Similar to a regular trigger wire, but depending on the configuration will wait x seconds before the trigger signal passes through.

1.Description: The time in seconds that it takes for signals to pass through this wire.
1.Name: DelayTime
SwitchValue
1.Description: Determines whether the switch is active or not.

Hatch.Description: Acts as a chute when active/gray, but when black or inactive it acts as a normal object.

Screen.Description: Allows the creation of GUI elements, programmatically. Very useful for creating custom interfaces.

1.Description: The ID of the camera feed being to be viewed, or 0 for none.
1.Name: VideoID

2.Description: Sets the PixelsPerStud on the SurfaceGui
2.Name: PixelsPerStud

Extractor.Description:
Harvests or mines materials from the world. It can extract things like grass, snow, wood, ores, etc depending on what terrain it is attached to.

Small resource-rich mountains can be found in the world, and these produce a number of unique resources such as Oil, Quartz, Silicon, and more.
You may want to configure the extractor to extract a specific resource, which you can do by setting the MaterialToExtract config, otherwise, it will select a random resource to mine.

1.Description: Determines the material to extract from connected natural surfaces. Disables the extractor if blank.
1.Name: MaterialToExtract

DevGenerator.Description: A debug item meant for developers.

BurstLaser.Description:
Fires 5 rapid sets of concentrated laser beams. Each beam does a mediate amount of damage.
Costs 100 power for each beam fired, meaning the total power cost is 500 power.

1.Description: The name of the limb that this Apparel is for.
1.Name: Limb

2.Description: The transparency of this Apparel.
2.Name: Transparency

Apparel.Description:
A piece of clothing that can be worn by other players. Parts can also be attached to the apparel, meaning you can create your own suits with the apprel.
It is similar to the prosthetic, except it can be taken off and does not cause damage. However, electricity does not trasmit throughout the apparel unlike prosthetics.

Apparel can also holds less parts than the prosthetic. It can only hold 100 parts, while Prosthetics can hold 150.

Apparel has another configuration to it called Transparency, which dictates how transparent it will become when worn. Ranges from 0-1 from non-transparent to transparent.

Cooler.Description:
Cools down the heat around a space when supplied with power. 
Glows blue while functioning. Can be used to provide a cool environment in hot areas. 
Is also useful for cooling down objects such as iondrives and engines.
Cooling amount is based on size -20 * X * Y * Z / 16

CloningBay.Description: Allows you to respawn at it from a remote location. Does not have to be locked, and only works if you are the person who crafted it. It can be reloaded via the model menu for other players to be able to use it.

1.Description: The name of the cloning bay.
1.Name: Name

Food.Description:
A consumable item.
*Appears* to be meat.
Upon clicking it, it will heal the user's health depending on the size.

Lead.Description: An uncommon material used in protection against radiation and weapon manufacturing. Has one of the lowest thermal conductivities of all elemental metals in the game, next to Titanium.

BlastingCap.Description: A component used in crafting recipes for more advanced explosive devices.

HeatPipe.Description: Allows for the transfer of heat. Use a HeatPump to direct the heat.

1.Description: The name of the material allowed to pass through.
1.Name: Filter

2.Description: Whether or not to invert the filter.
2.Name: Invert

Filter.Description: Similar to a chute and a pipe, but only allows the configured material to pass through.

1.Description: The ID of this antenna, to transmit to others with the same ID.
1.Name: AntennaID

Antenna.Description: A wireless transmitter that can transmit electricity from wires and trigger signals from trigger wires and buttons.

Instrument.Description:
A part that measures information about the world.

You can set it to measure one of:
Power - Total amount of power connected to the instrument.

Position - The position of the instrument in the world.
Orientation - The orientation of the instrument in the world.
Size - The size of the part attached to the instrument.

Speed - Speed of the instrument.
AngularSpeed - Angular speed of the instrument.

Temperature - The temperature of the instrument in Kelvin
TemperatureF - The temperature of the instrument in Fahrenheit.
TemperatureC - The temperature of the instrument in Celsius.
AirTemperature - The air temperature around the instrument in Kelvin.
AirTemperatureF - The air temperature around the instrument in Fahrenheit.
AirTemperatureC - The air temperature around the instrument in Celsius.

Time - The current region time.

1.Description: The type of instrument readout to display on the instrument.
1.Name: Type

ARController.Description:
Like a TouchScreen, but for your actual screen.
Has the capability to display augmented 3D objects and visuals in a virtualized world.
Click to equip/unequip. Output may only be displayed from one ARController at a time.

1.Description: The transparency of the AR display.
1.Name: Transparency
Coordinates
1.Description: The coordinates to your Destination.

3.Name: ForceLocalTeleport
3.Description: Whether to only attempt to teleport to teleporters within the same region, ignoring the "Coordinates" configuration.

2.Description: The ID of the teleporter at the goal coordinates to teleport directly to.
2.Name: TeleporterID

Teleporter.Description:
A device used to transport players across regions.
When powered and triggered, it will teleport all players in the beam to the given coordinates and teleporter id.
It will warp the player to a teleporter in the region with the given teleporter id.

When warping to a teleporter inside of a planet, set the last value to true. For example,
50, -50, 85, -75, true

Make sure you set the correct coordinates OR YOU WILL BE STRANDED!

Costs 1000 energy per teleport. Teleporter uses Energy regardless if a player is on the Teleporter at the moment it gets triggered.

Water.Description:
The basis of all life, and is a liquid found in terra, forest, ocean and certain tundras and rogue planets.
At 212 degrees, the water evaporates into steam.

Stick.Description: A natural resource found in trees and flora, often accompanied by wood. It is used for creating vital tools.

Laser.Description:
Fires a concentraded beam of energy when powered, which can be used to damage and set objects on fire. 
	Has a Range of 1000 studs.
	Primarily used as a weapon in space combat situations.
	While it can damage objects effectively, it cannot damage energy shields.

1.Name: DamageOnlyPlayers
1.Description: Determines if this laser is only allowed to damage players and not materials.

Goo.Description: A sticky substance that binds things together like glue. The effect lasts for for two minutes, but it can be washed off with Water. It will also melt off at 95 °F.

WaterCooler.Description: Removes -100 heat from the surrounding area, when supplied with power. Performs the same amount of cooling that five coolers would, give or take.

ReinforcedGlass.Description: A stronger, slightly less malleable version of glass. Blocks radiation.

BurnerGenerator.Description: Creates electricity when fueled with coal.

TestStarMap.Description:
A developer version of the starmap.

Showcases the entire universe. Lag maybe?? :topkek:

1.Description: Whether or not the gravity generator is enabled.
1.Name: Enabled

3.Description: The radius of the generated gravity field.
3.Name: Radius

2.Description: The amount of gravity within the influence of the GravityGenerator as a force.
2.Name: Gravity

DevGravityGenerator.Description: A debug item meant for developers.

Fence.Description: A metal fence. Can be used to set up walls and guard structures and bases.

Servo.Description:
Spins objects attached to the hinge at the front when powered, to set angles.
Polysilicon can be used to control its angle.
Activate will increment the goal angle by the configured angle step (clockwise looking at its face)
Deactivate will decrement the goal angle (counter-clockwise)
FlipFlop will reset the angle to 0
Microcontrollers can also set a servo's angle with :SetAngle(Goal)

1.Description: Determines the speed at which the servo is driven.
1.Name: ServoSpeed

4.Description: The target angle of the servo.
4.Name: Angle

3.Description: Determines how fast the servo attempts to correct its angle.
3.Name: Responsiveness

2.Description: Determines the change in angle when a pulse is received by Polysilicon.
2.Name: AngleStep

1.Name: Reversal
1.Description: Determines whether the output should be reversed.

2.Description: The ratio of speed from 1 (1:100) to 100 (100:100) between this DriveBox and the source motor.
2.Name: Ratio

DriveBox.Description:
When connected to a motor or engine with a rod, it will spin the same speed the engine or motor is going.
(You must click the drivebox first when creating a rod.)

MustardGas.Description: A heavy chemical warfare weapon used to damage organisms. Gas Masks nullify the effects of this gas.

ScubaMask.Description: A set of goggles which can be used to help vision while underwater.

MonsterMashPotion.Description: You'll be a graveyard smash with this thrilling dance potion.

TimeSensor.Description:
When the current time matches the time configured in the TimeSensor, it will send a trigger signal.

For example, if the world turns 7:15 it will send a trigger signal.

This is useful for creating dynamic lights that turn on only during the night, saving energy.

The format should be hour:minute

1.Description: The time at which this sensor will trigger.
1.Name: Time

ElectricFence.Description: A special version of the fence which damages upon contact as long as it is powered. Conducts electricity like a wire.

ARGlasses.Description:
Like a handheld Microcontroller, with a TouchScreen for your actual screen.
Has the capability to display augmented 3D objects and visuals in a virtualized world.

1.Name: Code
1.Description: The code to be executed on this microcontroller.

4.Description: The ID of the router network to connect to.
4.Name: RouterID

3.Description: The ID of the antenna network to connect to.
3.Name: AntennaID

2.Description: The transparency of the AR display.
2.Name: Transparency

1.Description: The name of the liquid to extract using the pump.
1.Name: LiquidToPump

Pump.Description: Pumps liquid from the environment into attached Tanks. For example, a pump located in the ocean will pump water when powered.

Torch.Description: A torch which can be used to provide light.

Assembler.Description: Assembles items as configured when the structure is supplied with the required power and resources.

1.Name: Assemble
1.Description: The name of the object to be assembled.

Diode.Description: Acts as a wire/chute/pipe/etc, but only works one way, through the diode's input and output faces as indicated by the arrow.

Neon.Description: A building decoration material that glows by itself without requiring power.

Keyboard.Description:
Similar to a button, except is programmable to take more than one key input.
Can be attached to a vehicle seat or clicked by a player.

Cement.Description: A modern material useful for pavement.

ImpactPlate.Description:
EXPERIMENTAL - Distributes the damage it takes between itself and parts attached to its top surface, with higher health parts absorbing the most damage.
**25%** resistance to kinetic damage (guns, blades, cannons, explosions).
Cannot be chained with other `ImpactPlate`s.

EnergyGun.Description: Fires a powerful shot of energy when provided power and triggered.

LightBridge.Description: Fires a beam of solid light that can be walked on.

1.Description: The color of the bridge's beam.
1.Name: BeamColor

ProximityButton.Description: Sends trigger signals when interacted via its ProximityPrompt. Key cannot be configured to 'W', 'A', 'S', 'D', or 'Space'.

1.Description: The name of the key that will trigger the proximity prompt on a keyboard.
1.Name: KeyboardKeyCode

3.Description: The text of the proximity prompt.
3.Name: ObjectText

2.Description: The name of the key that will trigger the proximity prompt on a gamepad.
2.Name: GamepadKeyCode

5.Description: The range of the prompt, from 0 - 50.
5.Name: MaxActivationDistance

4.Name: HoldDuration
4.Description: The length of time that the proximity prompt has to be held down for.

6.Name: RequiresLineOfSight
6.Description: Whether a line of sight to the center of the part is required for the prompt to become visible.

WirelessButton.Description: Similar to a button, but can be clicked from infinite distances and cannot be used for keybinds.

DarkConverter.Description: Converts attached dark matter bins into energy. 1 unit of dark matter is equal to 1000 watts of power. However, this generates a ton of heat in the process, nearly up to 200 degrees when activated. This means you will need about 10 coolers to avoid combustion.

Beacon.Description:
Creates a small beacon of light when powered. 
	When 'ShowOnMap\' is enabled, it broadcasts a signal into the universe.
	\'BeaconName\' changes the name of the beacon shown on the starmap. 
	30 second cooldown for changing the configurables.

1.Description: The name of the beacon.
1.Name: BeaconName

2.Name: ShowOnMap
2.Description: Whether this beacon should be shown on StarMaps.

LightTube.Description: Emits light when powered with electricity. Can be colored in different ways, changing the light color

1.Name: Shadows
1.Description: Whether or not the light will cast shadows.

SteamTurbine.Description: Produces power from steam at a base rate of 100 power each. Improves up to 250 per steam if consecutively ran at max speed. All bonuses are capped to the real consumption rate, so more steam equals better efficiency, but faster consumption rates. It may consume +0.5/s^2 steam, up to a maximum rate of 10 steam per second (for a total of 2500 power per second). Has a 10% chance to recover water for every steam consumed, improving up to 20%. Maximum efficiency can be reached in no less than 18 seconds if fed an optimal amount of steam.

Component.Description: A portable component. May be installed on parts to add unique behaviours.

Brick.Description: A cheap, malleable material with special durability properties. The durability is 4, and becomes 18 when it is anchored or attached to terrain (grounded).

Warhead.Description:
Causes a powerful explosion when triggered. You can use a delay wire to make it explode after a few seconds and not immediately.
The only down-side of the warhead is that it is blocked completely by energy shields.

AdBoard.Description: Allows the creation of Ad elements, automatically. Very useful for making money.

Transformer.Description: Sends a constant trigger signal when powered. By default, it will send a trigger signal every tick, but can be configured up to every 360 seconds. If the transformer's loop time matches the game's internal tick rate (the default,  0/s), it will synchronize with the game loop.

1.Description: The time in seconds between triggers.
1.Name: LoopTime

Fireworks.Description: Causes an explosion when triggered. You can use a delay wire to make it explode after a few seconds and not immediately.

CornerRoundWedge.Description: A rounded corner shaped template object.

FactionHub.Description:
Configures faction settings, view members, invite players, accept invites, save resources/models and view controlled regions.
		
		This is not a form of claiming a region.

1.Name: SwitchValue
1.Description: Determines whether the switch is active or not.

TriggerRelay.Description: Allows trigger/poly signals through when active, and blocks them when inactive. Unlike a regular TriggerSwitch, poly signals will NOT change its state.

ShapeRemover.Description: A template object which removes object shapes.

EnergySword.Description: A short ranged melee weapon which forms its own gravitational field when lunged. Forged with incarnated ̶m̶a̶g̶i̶c science!

Transistor.Description: Carries trigger signals in the direction of the arrow if any power source is attached. Can be inverted by clicking or configuring.

1.Name: Inverted
1.Description: Whether or not the state will be inverted.

Treads.Description:
Moves against surfaces it contacts. In order for the treads to function, you need to use a Motor, Engine, or DriveBox to spin up a part which will act as the driver part. The driver part should be connected to the treads via a rod, and should spin with the same orientation as a wheel would to achieve maximum speed.

Multiple driver parts can be attached to the treads at once, and their speeds will be added together. The treads will move depending on the direction & speed that the driver part spins.

The speed the treads move depends entirely on the speed of rotation on the axis perpendicular to the treads, so rotating the driver part off-axis will reduce (or invert) the speed. For example, 45 degrees off-axis = 50% speed, 90 degrees off-axis = 0% speed, 135 degrees off-axis = -50% speed, and 180 degrees off-axis = -100% speed.

Marble.Description: A compact, durable material. Primarily decorative.

CrudeWing.Description:
Creates lift from being pushed forward.
A worse version of a Wing.
Does not work in space or in non atmospheric planets.

Quartz.Description: A translucent and malleable crystal useful for making durable windows.

Primer.Description: A component used in crafting recipes for a few objects.

Katana.Description: A weeaboo sword used to cut down your enemies.

Plutonium.Description: A highly radioactive compound used in manufacturing nuclear explosives.

HeatPump.Description: Pumps Heat between two points. Pumps a maximum of **1 MW** of heat energy.

1.Description: How many kW of heat energy to pump.
1.Name: TransferRate

Speaker.Description:
Plays audio of length up to 5 seconds, unless it is powered in which case it can play a full audio.
When clicked or triggered, it will toggle playing music and will play the song id you give it.
Speaker:LoadSound(SoundId) will return a Sound object
A Sound object can be modified using properties SoundId, Looped, PlaybackSpeed, Pitch, TimePositionand the methods Play, Pause, Stop, Destroy

1.Description: The audio asset ID to be played.
1.Name: Audio

3.Description: The volume the audio plays at. The maximum volume is determined by the size of the speaker.
3.Name: Volume

2.Description: The pitch at which to play the audio.
2.Name: Pitch

Cloth.Description: A soft thin fabric that can soak up liquids.

Stone.Description: A resource found in nearly all planets. It is not recommended to use for structures, but is often used in crafting simple objects.

SoundMuffler.Description: A SoundMuffler will silences the sounds of machinery around it.

Hull.Description: A legacy pre-component part. Is able to float in the water, as well as carry objects attached to it. Primarily used for creating boats and other water craft.

VehicleSeat.Description:
Allows players to control vehicles by rotating when sat on.
It is incredibly important to have when creating vehicles.

Attaching buttons to the vehicleseat will allow the player sitting on it to trigger the button by pressing a key.
Simply attach the button to the vehicle seat, configure it to the keybind you would like, and it will allow you to trigger that button by pressing the key when sitting down in the seat.

1.Description: The speed at which the seat will rotate.
1.Name: Speed

3.Name: Enabled
3.Description: Determines whether this seat should control its rotation. Turning this off results in a regular seat.

2.Description: The control mode of the seat. Horizontal: Rotate horizontally with A/D. Full: Rotate horizontally and vertically with W/A/S/D. Mouse: point towards the player's mouse when holding click.
2.Name: Mode

RoundWedge.Description: A block rounded on one edge, or 1/4 of a cylinder.

Winch.Description:
A special device used to control the length of constraints attached to it.
When attaching a constraint to the Winch, click the Winch first.
When triggered with polysilicon, it will increase (Activate) or decrease (Deactivate).

1.Description: The length change in studs when triggered by Polysilicon.
1.Name: DeltaLength

3.Description: The maximum length in studs of the rope.
3.Name: MaxLength

2.Description: The minimum length in studs of the rope.
2.Name: MinLength

TriggerWire.Description: Allows trigger objects to interact with each other when connected by triggerwires.

RTG.Description: Creates electricity from decaying radioactive elements.

1.Description: The ID of this transporter, to transmit to others with the same ID.
1.Name: TransporterID

Transporter.Description:
Acts as an antenna but for bins and objects containing materials such as liquids and solids. 
Useful for creating large factory bases with many extractors without using long chutes.

Controller.Description:
Alters the speed of attached Controllable objects which include: Engine, Motor, BallastTank, IonDrive, IonRocket, Thruster, Rocket. Must use a polysilicon between this controller and 
	an object that emits a trigger signal(like a button) to use the same events as clicking the UI. For example, FlipFlop will set the speed of the Controllable objects to 0, Deactivate will subtract 5 from the current speed, etc.

Obelisk.Description:
An object designed to attract aliens to the region. Emits an ominous noise when powered.
Must be anchored and powered in order to function. Must also be open to the sky. Only one obelisk in a region can be powered at a time.
When active, it will summon aliens every 300 seconds.
**Use at your own risk.**

Motor.Description: Spins objects attached to the hinge at the front when powered.

1.Description: Determines the amount of power used to drive the motor. This affects the torque and power consumption. Negative values are reverse.
1.Name: Power

2.Description: Determines the gear ratio applied to the motor in terms of the multiplier on the RPM. A value of 0.1 indicates a 10:1 ratio, where RPM is 1/10th and torque is 10x when compared to the default setting of 1.
2.Name: Ratio

Aluminum.Description: A light, non-durable material. Has a good thermal conductivity, but is lower than most other metals.

Telescope.Description:
A device that allows you to see and query information about other regions and planets in space while powered.
To view a specific coordinate, configure the telescope and set to the desired coordinates, and then click the telescope.
The telescope will consume 15 power when looking up a coordinate.

The Telescope provides region information including but not limited to the following:
- Resources on the planet
- The planet's temperature
- The planet's distance from its star
- The type of planet

1.Name: ViewCoordinates
1.Description: The coordinates to view.

BlackBox.Description:
Records all activity in the region using very delicate instruments.
Does not function past 10000studs.

Blackbox Statuses:
    - OFFLINE = Blackbox is not locked.
    - TOO FAR = Blackbox is too far away.
    - ONLINE = Listening for event/Sharing event data
    
Blackbox Events:
    - Irradiated [(playerName) was irradiated]
    - Suffocating [(playerName) has no breathable air]/[(playerName) is breathing Carbon Dioxide]
    - Freezing [(playerName) is freezing]/[(playerName) is getting toasty]
    - Spawned [(playerName) teleported to region]
    - Death [(playerName) died.]
    - HyperDrive is warping to [(coordinate)]
    - Aliens were spawned from an obelisk located at [(position)]

Reactor.Description:
Generates steam using water and heat from radiation.
Up to 4 pieces of uranium can be inserted into the reactor as fuel.
If the temperature is above 400, it will begin to turn water into steam (rate dependent on temperature).
If the temperature exceeds 1200 F, a meltdown will occur.
The Reactor fuel status can be acquired through the :GetFuel() method with a microcontroller.
Polysilicon is used to control a reactor, and fuel must be ejected manually:

Activation lowers the control rods, decreasing reaction rate.
Deactivation raises the control rods, allowing fuel to react.
FlipFlop will eject fuel or waste from the fuel rod with the least fuel.

1.Name: Alarm
1.Description: Determines whether the reactor alarm system is enabled for when the reactor is near meltdown temperature.

2.Name: TriggerWhenEmpty
2.Description: Determines whether or not the reactor will emit a trigger signal when its fuel is empty.

1.Description: The name of the limb that this Prosthetic is for.
1.Name: Limb

Prosthetic.Description:
An artificial part that can be attached to players in exchange for a limb.
The limb configuration can be configureed to be the limb you want to have for a prosthetic, for example configuring it to be "Right Leg" will have the prosthetic attach itself to your character.
Simply touch the prosthetic, and it will automatically be attached to your body. This process is extremely unhealthy, however, and may result in short-term complications.

Parts can be attached to the prosthetic, allowing many uses for the prosthetic limb.

Prosthetic limbs are also electrically conductable, acting as a wire.

Heavily damages the character once attached.
Prosthetics can't have more than 50 parts attached to them.

RoundWedge2.Description: A block rounded inwards on one edge.

Decoupler.Description:
When triggered, it breaks welds and falls off of anything attached.
Can be used to separate things.
The trigger signals will pass through the decoupler as it is decoupled.

Solenoid.Description: Controls the switch state of any switches attached to its output face based on whether or not it has power in the configured range.

1.Name: Inverted
1.Description: Whether or not the state will be inverted.

3.Description: The kind of resource to check for.
3.Name: Resource

2.Name: Range
2.Description: The power range the state will be active for.

DevSink.Description: A debug item meant for developers.

1.Name: Resource
1.Description: The name of the object to produce a sink for.

Tile.Description: A cheap material made from baked clay useful for building houses.

1.Name: SwitchValue
1.Description: Determines whether the switch is active or not.

TriggerSwitch.Description: Allows trigger/poly signals through when active, and blocks them when inactive. Poly signals will change its state. Use a TriggerRelay if you need to work with poly signals.

SolarPanel.Description:
Generates electricity using solar energy from a local star. 
The closer it is to a star, the more energy it generates. 
The type of star also affects its energy generation, as well as the size of the solar panel. 

If the solar panel is blocked by a part, it will not generate any energy. Glass however will work.

Boombox.Description: Must be powered in order to play music. When clicked, it will toggle playing music and will play the song id you give it.

1.Name: Audio
1.Description: The audio asset ID to be played.

RepairKit.Description: A useful kit of tools that can be used to repair objects which have been damaged. Keep away from biters.

PDW-X44.Description: A versatile automatic pulse based PDW capable of dishing incredible amounts of damage in a small amount of time. Equipped with 3 barrels for an unparalleled firerate.

FactionSpawn.Description: Acts as a spawn location for the faction of the player who locked it.

DeleteSwitch.Description: An object that deletes itself when triggered.

1.Description: Determines the strength of the magnet.
1.Name: Strength

2.Description: Determines the maximum force applied by the magnet.
2.Name: MaxForce

SpawnPoint.Description: Acts as a spawn location for the player who locked it.

Rubber.Description: A textile resource (with GRASS not GLASS in the recipe) used in manufacturing many industrial objects.

Scrapper.Description: Scraps unlocked solid items into their crafting components (with some loss) on contact when powered, else destroys them if unpowered. Will send locked single raw parts such as Iron or AlienCore into connected bins.

TemperatureGate.Description:
The gate will allow power to pass through it while the temperature is in a certain range. 
It can be used in conjunction with a Transistor part to control the flow of generated trigger signals based on its temperature. 

Like the TemperatureSensor part, it will also use the attached Reactor temperature if there is one. 

Unlike the TemperatureSensor part, this one updates at a much faster 20 tps instead of 0.5 tps.

1.Description: The range of temperatures (°F) within which the gate will be open.
1.Name: TemperatureRange

3.Name: SwitchValue
3.Description: Determines whether the switch is active or not.

2.Description: Whether or not the state will be inverted.
2.Name: Inverted

Gun.Description:
Fires a harmful bullet when triggered.
Must be supplied with ammo in order to function.
For example, you need an iron bin with 1 or more iron directly attached to it to work.

Flamethrower.Description: Shoots a stream of flaming gasoline to ignite your foes.

Steam.Description: A result of water being heated up to high temperatures.

1.Description: The buoyancy of this Balloon, 0 being neutral.
1.Name: Buoyancy

Balloon.Description:
Levitates parts attached to it to a certain configurable height.
However, it is easily poppable.
Does not work in space, or no-atmosphere planets.

VitalScanner.Description: Displays chemicals another player has absorbed.

Stanlium.Description: Its love quivers, like it yearns for something within them; an eerie siren song that penetrates souls and tells of the destruction.

Kiln.Description: Turns attached sand bins into glass.

Glass.Description: Created when sand is burned, set on fire, or fed into a Kiln. Can be broken by heavy impacts or by fist.

SolarScoop.Description:
Extracts materials from a star when powered and pointed at a star.
Depending on the class of the star, it will extract more materials.

Generates around 240 degrees of heat, meaning you will need atleast 12 coolers to cool it down.

Red stars generate 25 helium, 5 plasma and 10 hydrogen per second.
Orange stars generate 30 helium, 5 plasma and and 15 hydrogen per second.
Yellow stars generate 35 helium, 5 plasma and and 20 hydrogen per second.
Light blue stars generate 40 helium, 25 hydrogen, 10 plasma and and 10 iron per second.
Neutron stars generate 60 helium, 45 hydrogen, 15 plasma and and 20 iron per second. It also generates 1-2 neutronium every 2 minutes.

It is recommended to use a Filter to seperate the materials extracted by a solar scoop.

Rail.Description:
Slides and moves objects along its surface when powered and triggered. Useful for creating retractable pistons and actuators, for turrets or other retractable devices.
		
Rails will only move objects connected on the relative top surface of the rail.
		
The rail can only be activated through the use of polysilicons.
Mode 0 or activating polysilicons will set the rail to position1.
Mode 1 or deactivating polysilicons will set the rail to position2.
Mode 2 or flip flop polysilicons will act like a switch, setting to position2 if position1 and vice versa.
		
Has 2 configurations, position1 and position2.
		
Both configurations should be between 0 and 100. These are percents of where the attached objects should slide to.
For example, if a rail was 50 studs long and position2 was 50 or 50%, the attached objects will slide to the middle or at 25 studs.
		
Due to roblox physics, rails may act weirdly. To prevent this from happening, you should always place your rails first before anything else. It is recommended to attach objects on the rail after the rail is safely placed down.

1.Description: Determines the position of the first state of the rail.
1.Name: Position1

3.Description: Determines the time it takes for the rail to change positions.
3.Name: TweenTime

2.Description: Determines the position of the second state of the rail.
2.Name: Position2

RepairLaser.Description: Fires a beam that repairs objects. Repairs **1** HP/s.

1.Description: The mode of the Polysilicon. Each mode results in different behaviors for objects.
1.Name: PolysiliconMode

2.Description: The amount of times to activate the Polysilicon from a single trigger.
2.Name: Frequency

Polysilicon.Description:
An electronic material which transforms a trigger signal into special on/off/toggle signals.

Has a configuration called Frequency which dictates how many times the polysilicon will repeat a trigger.
For example, if a polysilicon was attached to a pulley, having a frequency of 5 and triggered, the pulley will be activated 5 times.

1.Description: The buoyancy of this BallastTank, 0 being neutral.
1.Name: Buoyancy

2.Description: The offset from the surface of the water the ballast tank will try to maintain.
2.Name: BallastLevel

BallastTank.Description: Allows for variable ballast to be added to sea vehicles. Also prevents corrosion to attached parts underwater.

Pulverizer.Description:
Pulverizes resources into powdered forms. Power cost: 3/s.

---

**Recipes:**

- 1x **Ice** → 1x **Snow**

- 1x **Quartz**,1x **Stone** → 2x **Sand**

Gear.Description: A mechanical component commonly used in crafting recipes for many objects.

Furnace.Description: Burns resources at 16x speed to produce Heat energy directly. Has a low thermal conductivity.

Cannon.Description:
Fires a cannon ball when triggered or clicked.
Must be supplied with an ammo material.
Iron is prioritized, and results in one large cannonball being shot.
Copper results in grapeshot.

DevSource.Description: A debug item meant for developers.

1.Name: Resource
1.Description: The name of the object to produce a source for.

CornerRoundWedge2.Description: A corner shaped template object rounded inwards.

Tetrahedron.Description: A tetrahedron template made of 3 perpendicular right triangles.

Pipe.Description: Provides a medium for the transfer of liquids and gases between Tanks and other objects.

EthernetCable.Description: Allows for the transfer of data between ports. Mostly utilized in programming.

Faucet.Description: Releases liquids and gases from Tanks.

1.Description: Which kinds of resources to drop, separated by commas.
1.Name: Filter

NightVisionGoggles.Description: A set of goggles which can be used to see in the dark.

Thruster.Description:
A high powered propulsion device. The larger the thruster, the faster it can go, up to 500s/s, but it will consume more power.
The thruster will not operate below -30, or above 200 degrees fahrenheit.

1.Description: Determines the percentage of thrust (speed). Affects fuel consumption.

Billboardium.Description: A super strong alloy made of Robux and pure refined ad

SmoothGlass.Description: A version of Glass using the Roblox Glass material. Additionally can be templated.

TouchScreen.Description:
A Screen, but can handle player mouse input.
This is to be used with programming.

1.Description: The ID of the camera feed being to be viewed, or 0 for none.
1.Name: VideoID

2.Description: Sets the PixelsPerStud on the SurfaceGui
2.Name: PixelsPerStud

HeatCell.Description:
Legacy test item. Stores heat energy.
Has a limit of 400 kJ.

1.Description: The ID to transmit the camera feed over, received by screens of the same ID.
1.Name: VideoID

Camera.Description:
It's a camera.
When a camera and Screen have the same ID, that screen will be used to display the camera view.
Clicking on a screen that is displaying the view of a camera will allow you to directly view what the camera is seeing.
No power is necessary.

Juyicebire.Description: Juyicebire is a solid material found in space. It also has large sizes. It is an incredibly durable material. Upon contact with Steam, it will explode.

Scanner.Description: An end-game part which can remotely retrieve Microcontroller references to parts, providing information and control. Can also triangulate the positions of enemy parts given enough well placed scanners.

1.Name: Range
1.Description: The default range to scan for parts within.

Gasoline.Description: A liquid used for fueling many devices such as rockets and engines.

ImpulseCannon.Description: Blasts a harmless burst of energy which sends anything nearby soaring at a high velocity.

CornerTetra.Description: A template which is a tetrahedron subtracted from a cube.

Modem.Description: A part that allows you to send messages cross-region and make HTTP requests to the web.

1.Description: The ID of the network this modem should connect to.
1.Name: NetworkID

TemperatureSensor.Description:
When the surrounding temperature is within the defined range, it will emit a trigger signal every two seconds.
When connected to a Reactor part, will use the Reactor's internal temperature.

The more advanced twin of this part, the TemperatureGate part may be more useful in many cases.
It updates at a quicker rate and is more versatile, due to it controlling power flow.

1.Name: TemperatureRange
1.Description: The range of temperatures (°F) which this sensor will trigger at.

Melter.Description: Melts Ice into liquid Water by consuming Power.

Coal.Description: A natural resources commonly used as a source of generating heat and energy. Can be placed in a BurnerGenerator to generate simple and fast energy.

Cleat.Description: A textile resource similar to Rubber, except it has a high amount of friction and low bounciness. It can be used in physical machines such as the feet of mechs.

ChemicalSynthiser.Description:
Synthesizes and mixes chemical compounds. Consumes matter out of attached bins in order to fuel the material synthesis.

1 Nitrogen + 3 Hydrogen = 2 Ammonia 
1 Ammonia + 1 Ethanol = Diethylamine
2 Hydrogen + 2 Oxygen = Hydrogen Peroxide
2 Hydrogen + 1 Oxygen = Watern
1 Sodium + 1 Chlorine = Salt
2 Oxygen + 1 Carbon = Carbon Dioxide
2 Nitrogen + 1 Oxygen = Laughing gas/N2O
3 Chlorine + 1 Ethanol + 1 Water = Chloral Hydrate
1 Potassium + 1 Water = Explosion
1 Sodium + 1 Oxygen + 1 Hydrogen = 1 Sodium-Hydroxide
2 Oil + 1 Sodium-Hydroxide = Napalm
1 Diethylamine + 1 Ammonia + 1 Lithium + 1 Phosphorus = Hallucinogenic Compound
1 Salt + 1 Lithium + 1 Silicon + 1 Hydrogen = Hallucinogenic Toxin
1 Ammonia + 1 Oil + 1 Oxygen = Cyanide
1 Chlorine + 1 Ammonia = Mustard gas
1 Lithium + 1 Mercury = Toxin
1 Fluorine + 1 Hydrogen + 1 Potassium + 1 Sulphuric Acid = Fluorosulfuric Acid
1 Fluorosulfuric Acid + 1 Hydrogen Peroxide + 1 Nitrogen = Nitric Acid

FireWood.Description: A version of wood that is able to burn longer, allowing it to be an efficient fire burning device.

Extinguisher.Description: A handy container with a spray nozzle to extinguish fires.

HalfSphere.Description: A half sphere shaped template object.

Turbofan.Description:
Generates thrust from crude Oil, similar to a Thruster.
If a motor is attached to the front, it instead acts like an engine and rotates it.

1.Description: Determines the speed at which the turbofan is driven, or the speed at which it travels.
1.Name: TurboFanSpeed

MiningLaser.Description:
Fires a beam at resource deposits that will mine them just like an Extractor can, allowing for mining while mobile.
The MiningLaser produces 2x the resources, but costs 5x more power to run.

1.Description: Determines the material to extract from the laser beam. Disables the laser if blank.
1.Name: MaterialToExtract

HyperDrive.Description:
A device used to travel at faster than light speeds to other regions of the universe. 
Simply input the coordinates to your destination and have a sufficient amount of fuel, and you'll be on your way to your destination.
To initiate warping, power the hyperdrive and trigger it. When warping, the hyperdrive will be anchored to prevent any movement.

The power required for warping will be dependent on the distance travelled, as well as the size of the object being transported.
The amount of power required will be displayed in the hyper drive, shown in the red text. 

All of the parts connected to the hyperdrive and every player sitting will be teleported, however any free floating parts or standing up players will be sucked into the vaccum of space, so be careful.

The red text at the bottom of the hyperdrive indicates how much power is needed to perform the jump.

Make sure the numbers on the hyperdrive is facing up to ensure correct stud alignment.

1.Name: Coordinates
1.Description: The coordinates to warp to.

CombustionTurbine.Description: Creates electricity when fueled by gasoline.

TintedGlass.Description: A material similar to Glass, but is tinted black on the front..

SteamEngine.Description: It acts similar to a motor, but is powered by Steam instead of electricity.

1.Description: Determines the speed at which the engine is driven.
1.Name: EngineSpeed

IonRocket.Description:
A simple, fast propulsion device which consumes power to produce thrust. Moves in the direction of the arrow.
Can travel up to 100s/s at maximum propulsion.

1.Description: Determines the speed traveled at, 0 being standstill. Affects fuel consumption.
1.Name: Propulsion

Magnesium.Description: A shiny gray solid that is flammable, randomly ignites when touching stone.

1.Name: SwitchValue
1.Description: Determines whether the switch is active or not.

Switch.Description: Acts as a wire when active/green, but when black or inactive it acts as a normal object. Must use a polysilicon to switch for trigger events.

Helium.Description: A light invisible odorless gas, floats up.

Petroleum.Description: A gas used for creating plastic.

Igniter.Description: Sets alight unlocked parts within the immediate vicinity when triggered. Range depends on the size.

Perfectium.Description: The perfect material. Unbreakable, very stretchable, but is impossibly rare. The very sight of it makes you wonder the imperfections of human beings.

1.Name: Resource

2.Name: CanBeCraftedFrom
2.Description: Determines whether this bin can be used by nearby players to craft objects.

Bin.Description:
Stores solid items such as Aluminum, Iron, Faucets, etc. 
Can store up to 1000 items. When destroyed, every item inside will also be destroyed. 
The value increases as more items are added to it.

Bins can also be used as crafting recipes, with the resources inside being used.
You can also configure a bin to prevent items from being crafted from it, allowing for bins to be strictly for machine storage.

Microcontroller.Description:
Runs limited Roblox luau code in an environment called "pilot.lua".
Triggering it with a polysillicon will either start, stop, or restart (FlipFlop mode) your code.
You can also click it to turn it on/off.

Microcontrollers consume power depending on the amount of CPU time you use, which is the number of milliseconds your code spends doing stuff.
Pauses and waits don't count towards your CPU time since they allow the game to continue on to go do other work.
One CPU unit costs 1 units of power.
If you don't have enough power your Microcontroller will pause.

Your code has a CPU limit, it can only spend up to 100 milliseconds every game tick. If you go over this limit it will pause until the next game tick.

You can press F9 to view WoS's client-side output. Any logs or errors from your Microcontrollers will appear there.

If you want to know about various globals you can use from Roblox's engine, you can take a look at Roblox's Developer Documentation and search for Roblox Globals and Lua Globals.
For more info, check the game's wiki, or look at one of the game's social platforms if it's linked at the bottom of the game page.

1.Name: Code
1.Description: The code to be executed on this microcontroller.

2.Name: StartOnSpawn
2.Description: Whether or not to start the Microcontroller when it spawns.

1.Description: The ID of this router, to transmit to others with the same ID.
1.Name: RouterID

Router.Description: A wireless transmitter that can transmit an ethernet connection.

Neutronium.Description: The most durable obtainable material in the game. It is a strange form of matter found from the crusts of neutron stars. Due to the nature of neutron stars, neutronium is the hardest known material as well as the densest known material in the universe.

Chute.Description:
Used to transfer solid resources between objects such as bins and extractors.
Chutes may also transport multiple resources at the same time, allowing for an entire factory to be connected through one chute system.

Ice.Description: A compact natural resource found in tundra planets and the top of a few mountains. It is a slippery material, and has very low friction which can be useful in some devices.

StarMap.Description:
Shows your current location in the universe and other nearby stars and celestial bodies.
Has 2 modes, universe and solar.
Universe mode shows your location in the universe, and solar mode shows your location in the solar system if you are in one.
Requires power in order to function. 
	
It also has unique icons for every celestial body type. Clicking on a Icon will set a all connected HyperDrive/Telescope to those coordinates.

When triggered with polysilicon, polysilicon 0 will set it to univesre mode, polysilicon 1 will set it to solar system mode, and polysilicon 2 will switch it.

Has two iterative functions that can be used with the microcontroller 'GetBodies' and 'GetSystems', e.g. for key, val in StartMap:GetBodies() do

1.Description: What the tool should do when clicking. Point mode will aim the handle at the mouse cursor.
1.Name: Swing

3.Description: The name of the tool.
3.Name: ToolName

2.Description: Determines when this Handle should send trigger signals.
2.Name: TriggerMode

Handle.Description: A handle which can be equipped when a player touches it, turning all connected parts into an equipable tool.

Disk.Description:
A programmable object capable of storing complex data.
**Be aware, while disks can store userdata & function values, it cannot save them.**

DevLightningNode.Description: A debug item meant for developers.

Battery.Description: A light part that contains 1200 energy and is prefilled. Cannot be recharged.

Sand.Description: An abundant resource that can be found in the shores of terra and forest planets, the sea floors of ocean planets and in the dunes of desert planets. When burnt, the sand becomes glass.

Flashlight.Description: A flashlight which can be used to provide light.

EnergyBomb.Description: Causes a powerful explosion when triggered. Often used in space combat as a means of a powerful missile or torpedo.

Coupler.Description: Will connect to nearby couplers with matching CouplerIDs when activated by Polysilicon. Deactivating via Polysilicon will detach two couplers. Repeatedly emits trigger signals when it is able to connect with another coupler of the same ID.

1.Description: The ID of this coupler.
1.Name: CouplerID

2.Name: AutoTrigger
2.Description: Whether or not the coupler should emit trigger signals while in range of another valid coupler.

StasisField.Description:
Creates a 500 stud radius field that prevents any parts or objects around it from being dragged.
This can be used alongside with a RegionCloaker to create public infrastructure to avoid trolling and such.
However, in order to function, the shield must be anchored/grounded, and nothing must be blocking above it. The shield is also extremely fragile.

1.Name: MobileButtonEnabled
1.Description: If enabled, creates a proximity prompt so mobile users get an on-screen button.

4.Description: How far away players can be to see/use the mobile prompt.
4.Name: MobileMaxDistance

3.Description: How long the mobile prompt must be held before triggering.
3.Name: MobileHoldDuration

2.Description: The text shown on the mobile on-screen prompt button.
2.Name: MobileButtonText

Button.Description:
Sends trigger signals when clicked by a player.
When connected to a seat and the input key is configured/configureed, the player sitting in the seat can activate the button by pressing the corresponding key.
TriggerMode 0: Trigger on key down
TriggerMode 1: Trigger on key up
TriggerMode 2: Trigger on key down and key up

1.Description: The ID of the teleporter at the goal coordinates to teleport directly to.
1.Name: TeleporterID

DevTeleporter.Description: A debug item meant for developers.

Lava.Description: A liquid used for fueling many devices such as rockets and engines.

Mandrillium.Description: An ancient artifact left behind from an alternate reality.

HeatSink.Description: LEGACY. Reduces the air temperature by **10 °F** (Produces **43.93641495425122 kW** of heat energy).

DarkMatter.Description: A very valuable material extracted from black holes and a few empty regions in space. Can be used to generate energy when supplied to a DarkConverter

1.Description: The range that it can detect an object. Must be between 0 and 1000.
1.Name: MaxDistance

2.Description: The range that it will trigger if it detect an object.
2.Name: TriggerAtDistance

ObjectDetector.Description:
Casts a ray on the face with the hole on it, returning data of the object the ray hits.

Microcontroller function "GetLastHitData" returns a table with data about the last object hit.

Piston.Description: More accurately a linear actuator. There is a rail among us

1.Description: Determines the position of the first state of the piston.
1.Name: Position1

3.Description: Determines the speed of the piston.
3.Name: Speed

2.Description: Determines the position of the second state of the piston.
2.Name: Position2

PlutoniumCore.Description: A volatile core close to going supercritical used in recipes for Nuclear explosives.

Spheroid.Description: A stretchable sphere shaped template object.

ConveyorBelt.Description: Moves objects ontop of it towards the front of the conveyor belt. Only moves when powered and anchored or attached to the ground.

1.Description: Determines the speed at which the conveyor will move items on top of it.
1.Name: ConveyorBeltSpeed

Propeller.Description:
Propellers propel forward when spun.
Forward direction indicated by white spot.
Does not work in space or non atmospheric planets.

1.Description: The text to display on the front of the sign. Rich text is allowed.
1.Name: SignText

4.Name: TextScaled
4.Description: Whether or not the text is scaled to fit.

3.Description: The font of the text on the sign.
3.Name: TextFont

2.Name: TextColor
2.Description: The color of the text on the sign.

Sign.Description: Displays text or images. To display an image, configure it to id:imageid

1.Name: SwitchValue
1.Description: Determines whether the switch is active or not.

Valve.Description: Acts as a pipe when active/gray, but when black or inactive it acts as a normal object.

Obamium.Description: An ancient artifact left behind from an alternate reality.

Radar.Description: An instrument that shows a 2D top-down representation of Earth.

Freezer.Description: Turns liquid Water into solid Ice at a high energy cost, expelling heat energy in the process.

RegionCloaker.Description:
Hides a certain region from players, making the coordinates not appear on their screen. 
	Region can only be un/cloaked every 25 seconds. So if you unpower the RegionCloaker(uncloaks), you must wait 25 seconds before powering it again to ensure the region gets cloaked.

Port.Description:
Currently only used in programming. Allows a microcontroller to interface with Objects.
	To do so, the Port must be between the microcontroller and the Part or microcontroller and the EthernetCable(to interface with objets further away from the micro).
	Like so:
	Microcontroller <-> Port <-> Part
			or
	Microcontroller <-> Port <-> EthernetCable <-> Part
	"<->" meaning it is directly touching.

1.Description: The ID of this port used to utilize this port by connected microcontrollers.
1.Name: PortID

AutomaticLaser.Description: Fires a continous set of lasers when powered. Like most other energy/thermal weapons, it generates heat when powered. It generates up to 65 degrees of heat, meaning you will need atleast 2 or 3 coolers.

Relay.Description:
A powerful transmitter capable of transmitting trigger signals and resources/power between different regions.
It is a more powerful version of the antenna and transporter.

Unlike the antenna, the relay has 2 modes, mode 0 and mode 1.
Mode 0 sends resources/power and trigger signals, while mode 1 receives it.

Unlike the antenna, it can also transfer power in inactive regions or regions without players in them.
This means that you can connect a relay to your main base, warp away without anyone in the base, and still have the relay get the sufficient amount of power.

However, you should have only one sending relay per coordinate, as conflicts can occur if there are 2 or more relays in the region/coordinates sending power or signals with the same ID.
On the other hand, there can be an infinite number of receivers but the power/resources will be distributed evenly among them.

For example, let's say a relay network has a total output of 500 power and 25 iron. If there are 5 active receivers, each of them will get 100 power and 5 iron.

When the relay is red, it means it not functioning. When it turns green, it is properly linked up to another relay or is sending signals.

1.Description: The mode of the relay. Send outputs materials to other receiving relays; Receive receives materials from sending relays.
1.Name: Mode

2.Description: The ID of the relay, to send or take materials to or from other relays with the same ID.
2.Name: LinkerID

DarkReactor.Description:
Generates Dark Matter when powered and near a black hole.
The reactor is very unstable, and if the reactor overheats it will cause a huge explosion.

The DarkReactor generates up to 500 degrees of temperature, meaing you will need atleast 25 coolers to cool the reactor to make sure it does not overheat.

Railgun.Description:
Fires a piercing rail at high speeds. A long range weapon. Requires rails and electricity for ammo. Damage increases for every 10 studs of length.
Will pierce if the hit part is destroyed. Must be at least have a width and height of 6 and at least a length of 30 to function.
	
While Railgun is similar to Artillery, the Railgun is nearly instant while Artillery is a projectile weapon.

Requires to charge for one minute before it can fire. While charging and when charged, it creates large amount of heat. Charging status resets when this part is damaged.

When it is finished charging, it will stop creating a sound. At that point, it must be triggered and supplied by a rail bin in order to fire.

1.Description: Which kinds of resources to drop, separated by commas.
1.Name: Filter

Sorter.Description: Moves a type of resource through it, depending on the input and output faces as indicated by the arrow. Behaves just like the old Diode part when set to insert 100 Power.

1.Description: The kind of resource to push. May be a special or generic type like Gas, Solid, etc.
1.Name: Resource

3.Description: How much of the resource to push when triggered. May be infinite.
3.Name: TriggerQuantity

2.Description: How much of the resource to push per second. May be inf (or math.huge in a Microcontroller).
2.Name: Rate

Wing.Description:
Creates lift from being pushed forward.
Works at higher altitudes and at better angles than a CrudeWing.
Does not work in space or in non atmospheric planets.

DevBattery.Description: A debug item meant for developers.

Flint.Description:
Useful for lighting up flammable materials.
Simply rub it against a flammable material and it will set it on fire.

Wire.Description: Allows electrical objects to interact with each other when connected by wires. For example, attaching a wire between a powercell and a light will allow electricity to move through the wire, allowing the light to function causing a source of light to be created.

Rifle.Description: A powerful long-range bolt action weapon. Q to scope.

StudAligner.Description: Snaps the entire assembly its attached to to the grid.

Tire.Description: A cylindrical shaped object used commonly in vehicles such as cars.

AdminTool.Description: A debug item meant for developers.

Diamond.Description: A rare, carbon-dense, and very durable gem. Takes 2x energy damage & allows lasers to pass.

Sail.Description: Utilizes the wind to move forward.

FloatDevice.Description: Produces a force which counteracts gravity and keeps the device floating. The device will additionally resist upwards and downwards vertical motion.

1.Name: SwitchValue
1.Description: Determines whether the switch is active or not.

HeatValve.Description: Acts as a HeatPipe when active/red, but when black or inactive it acts as a normal object.

AirSupply.Description: Generates a 300 stud radius oxygen bubble when powered on. Very important part for space ships, as it acts as the oxygen supply for the ship.

Constructor.Description:
Similar to an assembler, but constructs a model when triggered. However, the constructor must be supplied with the correct materials for a model.
For example, a car model requiring 50 iron and 30 wires will need a bin attached with 50 iron, a bin attached with 30 wires and 100 power.
		
You can find out how many materials you need through the model loader gui.
Has a 60 second cool down or a minute cooldown to prevent model spamming.

1.Name: ModelCode
1.Description: The model data of the model to be created by the Constructor.

3.Name: RelativeToConstructor
3.Description: Determines if the created model should be loaded in relative to the orientation of the Constructor.

2.Name: Autolock
2.Description: Determines if the created model should be locked by the owner of the Constructor.

tinnitus.Description: An interesting spring which does strange things. (unobtainable)

1.Description: The kind of resource the tank can hold. You can set this to Any to allow the tank to accept anything, and None to prevent the tank from being filled
1.Name: Resource

2.Name: CanBeCraftedFrom
2.Description: Determines whether this Tank can be used by nearby players to craft objects.

Tank.Description: Stores liquids and gases. When a liquid or gas touches the Tank, the Tank will automatically store it. Will not conduct heat when containing a fluid, making it a good heat storage part.

Heatshield.Description: Generates a 300 stud radius area that protects all players and **only players** within the vicinity from temperature damage.

Hydrogen.Description: A gas commonly found in stars and gas giants.

Rocket.Description: A propulsion device that consumes gasoline.

1.Description: Determines the speed traveled at, 0 being standstill. Affects fuel consumption.
1.Name: Propulsion

RemoteControl.Description: Sends trigger signals forward wirelessly when triggered. Supports all variants of trigger signals including from Polysilicon.

1.Description: The range in studs at which signals will be transmitted.
1.Name: RemoteControlRange

2.Description: The way in which trigger signals should be transmitted. This setting only affects parts that are connective to trigger signals (e.g. TriggerWire).
2.Name: RemoteControlMode

FluidProjector.Description:
A device which projects a field of gas or liquid in front of it which you can swim in.
Host the universe's greatest pool party!
The fluid area can be configureed in size and type.

The FluidProjector requires power in order to work, and must be supplied with the correct fluid to work.
Significantly more power is required on planets with high gravity.
As an example, if the fluid is water, it will need a supplied Tank of water attached to work.

1.Description: The size in studs of the projected fluid field.
1.Name: Size

2.Description: The name of the fluid being projected.
2.Name: Fluid

SmoothReinforcedGlass.Description: A version of ReinforcedGlass using the Roblox Glass material.

EnergyShield.Description:
Generates a forcefield protecting its interior from energy-based weapons such as Lasers and PlasmaCannons, and
    offers full protection from Warhead explosions.
    
    An EnergyShield has a few sets of properties that you can fine tune to create a balanced shield.
    ShieldRadius - The size of the entire shield. This will exponentially consume more power the higher the radius is.
    RegenerationSpeed - Scale from 1 to 10 on how fast the shield will regenerate. The shield will not regenerate while unpowered.
    ShieldStrength - Scale from 1 to 10 on how much the shield can endure.

    RegenerationSpeed and ShieldStrength combined must not exceed 11.

1.Description: The size of the entire shield. The shield exponentially consumes more power the higher this is.
1.Name: ShieldRadius

3.Description: Determines the shield's resistance to damage.
3.Name: ShieldStrength

2.Description: Determines how fast the shield regenerates after being hit.
2.Name: RegenerationSpeed

Boiler.Description: Consumes Coal and Water and produces Steam.

Jade.Description: Reduces damage taken by 1.5 to a minimum of 0.2, but takes 25% additional damage.

SubspaceTripmine.Description: WARNING: HIGH EXPLOSIVE DEVICE. When triggered, this devastating weapon rips a gashing hole in the fabric of reality - subsequent spacetime reification results in a large explosion. USE: Drop mine. Once the mine stops moving, it will enter subspace and become invisible. At this point the mine is armed. Touching the mine will set it off...

StorageSensor.Description:
When the number of contents within connected storage objects is within a defined range, it will send trigger signals similar to a button.
This can be used to automate production of certain products when the stored quantity is low.

1.Name: QuantityRange
1.Description: The range of item quantities within which this sensor will trigger.

Beaker.Description: A container for holding mixed chemicals.

Artillery.Description:
Fires a fast-moving metal shell upon being triggered.
This metal shell generates a small explosion upon impact.
Costs 15 iron per shot.

Light.Description: Emits light when powered with electricity. Can be colored in different ways, changing the light color

1.Description: The brightness of the light.

Gyro.Description:
Stabilizes vehicles and structures by pointing upwards. Useful for mechs or orientating structures to the correct rotation. Has a maximum range of 75000 studss. The gyro can also be configured to seek objects and players.


When powered, the gyro will follow its seek commands that can be configured using hammer.
The gyro has commands that allow it to find and seek objects and players. It also features command grouping allowing commands to take priority (checked left to right) or fallback commands if the first group fails. You can group commands using parenthesis, inner group are resolved first then outter groups. For examples read the rest of this page.

An example of gyro's seek configuration with the "Player" command includes "Player Player1,Player2" which will seek and aim towards the nearest player.

Putting "Radar" at the beginning of the seek configuration will make it target parts in that group. For example, "Radar Gold Copper" will find Gold or Copper objects, starting from left to right (so Gold first) regardless of distance (max range is still 75000).

To target ore deposits, use the "deposit" command followed by the deposit name, currently the default deposits are ["Iron","Aluminum","Gold","Copper","Diamond","Uranium","Jade","Coal","Uranium","Titanium","Lead"]. There could be more if you are in a region with RNG ores. If that's the case, use the RNG ores name as a deposit. Example: "deposit Iron" or RNG ore "deposit Amougus"

Putting "AllExcept" will make the seeker target everything except the given list, basically inverting it. For example, "AllExcept Player1,Player2" will target "Player3", "Player4", etc but not "Player1" and "player2".

The commands "Min" and "Max" set the minimum or maximum distance the seeker will target. For example, "Min20 Max500" will make the seeker only target objects within 500 studs and more than 20 studs away.

TriggerWhenSeeked will trigger all connected parts every second when the Seek configurable is satisfied

"TrigMin" and "TrigMax" work the same as "Min" and "Max" but it's for the trigger signal, trigger signal will only be sent if the above property is true.

Putting "Star" as part of the list will make the seeker automatically target the main stellar body in the system.

Gyros also have a property called MaxTorque. This allows you to control the max force on the gyro to stabilize it.


# Quick command guide (Seek):

- "Player AddictedProgramming" -> Seek that player.

- "Radar Gold" -> Seek Gold objects/parts instead of players.

- "CreatedBy AddictedProgramming" -> Only objects created by that user.

- "LockedBy AddictedProgramming" -> Only objects locked by that user.

- "Min20 Max500" -> Only seek targets between 20 and 500 studs.

- "TrigMin30 TrigMax300" -> Only Trigger if target is within the 30-300 range.

- "AllExcept Radar Gold" -> Locates all Objects except for gold
 
- "(Radar Gold (AllExcept Max20))" -> Gold, but not within 20 studs.
 
- "AllExcept Player1,Player2 TrigMin10 TrigMax50" -> Trigger when target is any player except Player1/Player2 and is between 10 and 50 studs.

- "(Nearest (Radar Gold) Iron)" -> Pick nearest result between Gold and Iron, Gold getting priority.


# Direction/orientation commands:

- "PointAt 0,100,0" -> Aim at world position.

- "PointAlong 0,1,0" -> Aim along a direction vector.

- "UpVector 0,0,1" -> Set custom up vector.

- "TargetSurface" -> Aim at closest point on target surface.

- "CheckSurface" -> Measure seek distance using target surface.

- "Star" or "Sun" -> Aim toward the system's main star.


# Examples:

- "(Radar Gold (CreatedBy AddictedProgramming))"

> Finds Gold created by AddictedProgramming.


- "(Nearest (Radar Gold CreatedBy AddictedProgramming) Iron)"

Checks if Gold created by AddictedProgramming is the nearest or if Iron is.


- "( (Radar Gold CreatedBy AddictedProgramming) Iron)"

Checks if Gold created by AddictedProgramming is found within the maximum range if not it checks for Iron, Gold will always have priority even if Iron is closer.


- "(Radar Gold LockedBy AddictedProgramming (AllExcept Max20))"

Finds Gold locked by AddictedProgramming, but excludes targets within 20 studs.

WindTurbine.Description:
Creates rotation using the wind.
Unreliable and large motor.
Does not work in space or no-atmosphere planets.

Rotor.Description:
Provides vertical height when spun, and only works in oxygen planets.
The spin speed determines the height, and the tilt of the rotor determines the forward propulsion of the rotor.

Explosive.Description: Causes an explosion when triggered. You can use a delay wire to make it explode after a few seconds and not immediately.

Radiator.Description: LEGACY. Emits heat by releasing photons, making it ideal for discarding heat, and cooling things down. Will raise the temperature of surrounding air by **2.25 °F/s** (**85%** of the input heat will be permanently discarded). Effectively gets rid of **56.02 kW** (1 kW is 1 kJ/s) of heat energy. In total, only **9.89 kW** of the heat energy it releases will re-enter any surrounding air. In space, all **65.9 kW** of the Radiator's throughput will be expelled.

Sulfur.Description: A yellow flammable solid which can be found in Stone deposits. Being set on fire gives it a special blue fire.

PowerCell.Description:
Stores electricity, and is used to power many devices using wires or by directly attaching it.
Has a maximum capacity of 200000.

Grass.Description: An organic substance found in terra and forest planets. Often green, but can be other colors. Useful for planting seeds for agriculture.

Shotgun.Description:
Fires a shot of harmful pellets when triggered.
Must be supplied with ammo in order to function.
For example, you need an iron bin with 1 or more iron directly attached to it to work.

Titanium.Description: A strong heavy material that is very useful for small scale constructs. Has a very low thermal conductivity, the lowest of all metals in the game.

Hologram.Description: Using our brand new Multi-Dimensional Holographic Projection Technology™ you are able to create a stationary clone with only the ID of the user provided!.

1.Description: The UserId of the player for the Hologram to display.
1.Name: UserId

TractorBeam.Description: Fires a beam that exerts force on the object it hits. More effective in space due to low gravity, but still decently strong when affected by gravity. Force is affected by size and configuration.

1.Name: PowerPercent

FourthOfJuly.Description: Causes an explosion when triggered along with a Fourth Of July message. You can use a delay wire to make it explode after a few seconds and not immediately.

AlienCore.Description:
A mysterious piece of technology found within many robotic aliens.
Although its precise function is unknown, it manages to be extremely useful in advanced technologies.
It seems to emanate raw power on its own, but only these robotic constructions seem to know .
Generally, more powerful aliens will utilize more alien cores.

Oil.Description: A liquid used in refineries to produce Gasoline which can be used for fueling engines and rockets and Petroleum which can be used to make plastic.

Uranium.Description:
A radioactive material often found in deposits in planets, especially ones near stars.
Useful for energy generation from reactors or radiation generators.

Asphalt.Description:
A modern material useful for smooth road surfaces.
Its durability triples when anchored.

PlasmaCannon.Description:
Fires an orb of unstable plasma out of the barrel exploding on impact.
Needs to be fueled with 500 power and 50 helium or 1 plasma to fire.

RepairPlate.Description:
EXPERIMENTAL - While at least **90%** charged (**27** power), distributes repaired health between itself and damaged parts attached to its top surface.

Charges at a fixed rate of **1** power per second, up to a total capacity of **30**. Once charged, it consumes **2.5** power per second.
Can be chained with other `RepairPlate`s.
Power cannot be inserted or extracted.
Cannot be resized below 1x1x1.
